reasoning: Both attempts get the ready-handshake ordering right, use per-player keys, and call `removeClient`. A uses the APIs the library facts verify (`Charm.signal` getter/setter, `VideCharm.useSignalState`), keeps the 50 limit and the state shape in one shared module, and is strictly typed. B relies on `Charm.atom` and `VideCharm.useAtom`, which the 0.11/0.4.1 facts do not confirm and which may not exist; it also bypasses typing with `any` casts and keeps two field lists that must stay in step. A is the safer merge.

criteria.note: `ServerScriptService/PlayerState.luau` keeps one `Charm.signal` keyed by Player and updates it by copying with `table.clone`; `onPlaceBlock` checks `PlayerState:Get(player).BlocksLeft <= 0`, and `PlayerRemoving` clears the entry.

`CharmSync.server.connect` is called once and fires `remote:FireClient(player, payloads)`; on the ready remote, `addSignalsToClient` subscribes the player under the per-player key `PlayerState-{userId}`, and `removeClient` runs on leave.
`StartAsync` calls `addSignals` with `setState` under the same key, connects `OnClientEvent` to `client.patch`, and only then calls `FireServer`, so the first full payload cannot be missed.

criteria.criterion: UI bridge, shared limit, initial display
criteria.note: `VideCharm.useSignalState` runs inside the mounted `app` scope; the limit is `BlockTypes.MaxBlocksPerPlayer`, shared by both sides, and the label shows 50 until the first payload.

criteria.criterion: UI never writes the synced signal
criteria.note: Client `PlayerState` exports only `getState`; `setState` is handed only to CharmSync.
Adding the next value means one new field in the shared `PlayerState` type and `DEFAULT_STATE`, which syncs under the same per-player key.

Files are `--!strict`, all checks pass, and the hotbar is moved into a `Hotbar` stack container with its layout preserved. The per-player `Charm.computed` from `GetSignal` is never disposed, a small leak.

Each player gets their own atom from `PlayerState.get`, dropped on `PlayerRemoving`. But `get` lazily creates state again if called after the player leaves, and `Charm.atom` is not the verified 0.11 `signal` API.

`server.connect` is called once and fires the remote to the player; `addSignalsToClient` uses per-player `field:userId` keys built by `keyAtoms`, and `removeClient` runs on leave. The `:: any` cast hides typing.
`addSignals` is called before `OnClientEvent` is connected and before `FireServer`, so the handshake ordering is right; registration passes the atoms through `PlayerState :: any`.

criteria.criterion: UI bridge, shared limit, initial display
criteria.note: The server syncs the remaining count, and the label stays hidden while the count is nil, which is sensible. The bridge is `VideCharm.useAtom`, which the vide-charm 0.4.1 facts do not confirm (only `useSignalState`).

criteria.criterion: UI never writes the synced signal
criteria.note: The client only reads the atom; the module is documented as read only.
Adding a value means a matching atom in both `PlayerState` modules, kept in sync by name only, with no shared type.
Checks pass, but the files are non-strict with `:: any` casts, and relying on `Charm.atom` and `useAtom` risks runtime errors in Charm 0.11.1 and vide-charm 0.4.1.

strengths: Uses the Charm `signal` getter/setter API and vide-charm `useSignalState`, both verified in the library facts
One shared definition of the state shape, the defaults, and the 50 limit
Ready handshake ordered correctly on the client
weaknesses: The per-player computed made in `GetSignal` is never disposed
Syncing the whole state table as one key means each patch diffs the full table (minor)

strengths: Per-player atoms and `keyAtoms` give a tidy per-field, per-player key scheme
Label is hidden until the server's first payload
weaknesses: Uses `Charm.atom` and `VideCharm.useAtom`, which do not match the verified Charm 0.11 `signal` and vide-charm `useSignalState` APIs
Client and server field lists can drift apart because there is no shared type
Lazy `get` can re-create state for a player who has already left
